loops1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which two hormones act on the collecting duct?
opts: Parathyroid hormone and calcitonin
These regulate calcium and are not the collecting duct hormones; aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone are.
Renin and angiotensin II
Renin and angiotensin II drive the renin-angiotensin system and stimulate aldosterone release; the collecting duct hormones are aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone.
Aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone
Correct. Aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone act on the collecting duct, controlling sodium and potassium handling and the water channels that decide how concentrated the urine is.
Insulin and glucagon
These control glucose and are not the collecting duct hormones; aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone are.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 11

loops1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which reflex changes follow the volume depletion caused by a loop diuretic?
opts: Decreased renin, aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone
These would worsen the volume loss; the reflex to volume depletion is a rise in renin, aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone.
Increased renin, aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone
Correct. Volume depletion drives a reflex rise in the renin-angiotensin system, aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone, which is why the kidney resists the diuretic.
Increased renin with decreased antidiuretic hormone
Antidiuretic hormone rises, not falls, with volume depletion; the reflex is more renin, aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone.
Decreased renin with increased aldosterone
Aldosterone follows renin, so both rise; the reflex to volume depletion is more renin, aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 15

loops1.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which two effects on uric acid explain why loop diuretics cause gout?
opts: More urate excretion and a diluted plasma level
That would lower uric acid; loop diuretics reduce excretion and concentrate the plasma level, raising the gout risk.
Less urate excretion and a concentrated plasma level
Correct. Loop diuretics increase proximal reabsorption and decrease tubular excretion of uric acid, and volume contraction concentrates the plasma level.
More urate production and a diluted plasma level
Loop diuretics do not increase production and volume contraction concentrates rather than dilutes; they reduce excretion and concentrate the plasma level.
Less urate production and a concentrated plasma level
Loop diuretics do not change urate production; the gout risk comes from reduced tubular excretion plus a concentrated plasma level.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 15

loops1.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which agent is a loop diuretic?
opts: Metolazone
Metolazone is a thiazide-type diuretic acting in the distal tubule; the loop diuretics are furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide and ethacrynic acid.
Bumetanide
Correct. Bumetanide (Bumex) is one of the four loop diuretics, along with furosemide, torsemide and ethacrynic acid.
Triamterene
Triamterene is a potassium-sparing diuretic; the loop diuretics are furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide and ethacrynic acid.
Methazolamide
Methazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor; the loop diuretics are furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide and ethacrynic acid.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 12

loops1.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which acid-base disturbance do loop diuretics cause?
opts: Metabolic alkalosis
Correct. Volume depletion and enhanced hydrogen ion secretion produce a mild metabolic alkalosis, called a contraction alkalosis.
Metabolic acidosis
Metabolic acidosis is the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor effect; loop diuretics cause a contraction alkalosis.
Respiratory acidosis
Respiratory acidosis comes from retained carbon dioxide and is not a loop diuretic effect; they cause a metabolic alkalosis.
Respiratory alkalosis
Respiratory alkalosis comes from overbreathing and is not a loop diuretic effect; they cause a metabolic alkalosis.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 16

loops1.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which patient history calls for caution with a loop diuretic because it can precipitate flares?
opts: Gout
Correct. Loop diuretics reduce uric acid excretion and concentrate it as volume contracts, so they can precipitate gout flares.
Pulmonary edema
Pulmonary edema is an indication for a loop diuretic; the history that calls for caution is gout.
Cirrhosis with ascites
Cirrhosis with ascites is an indication for a loop diuretic; the history that calls for caution is gout.
Nephrotic syndrome
Nephrotic syndrome is an indication for a loop diuretic; the history that calls for caution is gout.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 15

loops1.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Edema from which of these conditions is treated with a loop diuretic?
opts: Acute bacterial cystitis
Cystitis is a bladder infection treated with an antibiotic and does not cause edema; the edematous protein-losing condition treated with a loop diuretic is nephrotic syndrome.
Adrenal insufficiency
Adrenal insufficiency causes salt and water loss, not edema; the edematous protein-losing condition treated with a loop diuretic is nephrotic syndrome.
Diabetes insipidus
Diabetes insipidus is excess water loss from lack of antidiuretic hormone action, not edema; the edematous protein-losing condition treated with a loop diuretic is nephrotic syndrome.
Nephrotic syndrome
Correct. In nephrotic syndrome protein loss prevents regulation of plasma fluids, and loop diuretics remove the excess fluid.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 17

loops1.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which loop diuretic complication can lead to seizures?
opts: Hyperkalemia
Loop diuretics lower rather than raise potassium, and hyperkalemia causes arrhythmias; the seizure risk is hyponatremia.
Hypercalcemia
Loop diuretics increase calcium loss and do not cause hypercalcemia; the seizure risk is hyponatremia.
Hyponatremia
Correct. Losing too much sodium can cause hyponatremia, which can lead to seizures.
Hypermagnesemia
Loop diuretics increase magnesium loss and do not cause hypermagnesemia; the seizure risk is hyponatremia.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 18

loops1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which segment moves weak acids and weak bases into the tubular lumen?
opts: Collecting duct
The collecting duct is controlled by aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone; weak acids and bases are excreted into the lumen at the proximal tubule.
Distal convoluted tubule
The distal tubule reabsorbs about 5 percent of the sodium; the proximal tubule is where weak acids and bases are excreted into the lumen.
Descending limb of the loop of Henle
The descending limb is where water leaves the lumen; weak acids and bases are excreted into the lumen at the proximal tubule.
Proximal tubule
Correct. Weak acids and bases are excreted into the lumen at the proximal tubule, where most of the filtrate is also reabsorbed.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 8

loops1.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which of these is an indication for a loop diuretic?
opts: Volume depletion
Volume depletion is an adverse effect of loop diuretics, not an indication.
Ascites from cirrhosis
Correct. Cirrhosis of the liver with ascites is a listed indication for loop diuretics.
Hypokalemia
Hypokalemia is an adverse effect of loop diuretics, not an indication.
Contraction alkalosis
Contraction alkalosis is an adverse effect of loop diuretics, not an indication.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 17

loops1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which segment reabsorbs about a quarter of the sodium and is impermeable to water?
opts: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
Correct. The ascending limb reabsorbs about 25 percent of the sodium and is impermeable to water, so the sodium leaves without water following.
Descending limb of the loop of Henle
The descending limb is where water leaves the lumen; it is the ascending limb that reabsorbs about a quarter of the sodium and is impermeable to water.
Proximal tubule
The proximal tubule reabsorbs most of the filtrate with water following; the segment that reabsorbs about a quarter of the sodium and is impermeable to water is the ascending limb.
Collecting duct
The collecting duct reabsorbs only about 2 to 3 percent of the sodium, far less than a quarter; the ascending limb reabsorbs about a quarter and is impermeable to water.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 9

loops1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: In which segment is most of the filtrate reabsorbed?
opts: Loop of Henle
The loop of Henle concentrates urine and reabsorbs a quarter of the sodium, but the largest share of the filtrate is reabsorbed earlier in the proximal tubule.
Distal convoluted tubule
The distal tubule reabsorbs only about 5 percent of the sodium; most of the filtrate is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule.
Collecting duct
The collecting duct reabsorbs only about 2 to 3 percent of the sodium; the bulk of the filtrate is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule.
Proximal tubule
Correct. The proximal tubule reabsorbs about 60 to 70 percent of the filtrate, which is why little of the filtered volume ends up as urine.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 8

loops1.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: What is the concern when a patient taking lithium for bipolar disorder starts a loop diuretic?
opts: Faster lithium clearance and loss of effect
The interaction runs the other way; clearance falls and toxicity rises.
Reduced lithium clearance and toxicity
Correct. Loop diuretics decrease lithium clearance and increase its toxicity.
Reduced diuretic effect of the loop agent
The listed concern is lithium toxicity from reduced clearance, not a weaker diuretic effect.
Lithium-induced hypokalemia becoming fatal
The listed concern is reduced lithium clearance with toxicity, not a potassium effect of lithium.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 19

loops1.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: What do all diuretics have in common?
opts: They increase sodium chloride excretion
Correct. Diuretics are defined as drugs that increase urine flow and sodium and chloride excretion, and they differ only in where along the nephron they act.
They lower the glomerular filtration rate
Diuretics are defined by more urine flow and sodium chloride loss, not by lowering filtration; if anything, volume depletion can lower filtration as a side effect.
They raise plasma sodium concentration
Diuretics remove sodium and chloride in the urine, so they do not raise sodium; some can even lower plasma sodium, which is a risk, not the defining action.
They block aldosterone receptors
Only the aldosterone antagonists block aldosterone receptors; the class as a whole is defined by increasing urine flow and sodium chloride excretion.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 4

loops1.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which loop diuretic is marketed under the brand name Lasix?
opts: Bumetanide
Bumetanide is sold as Bumex; furosemide is the loop diuretic sold as Lasix.
Furosemide
Correct. Furosemide is sold as Lasix; the other loop diuretics are bumetanide (Bumex), torsemide (Demadex) and ethacrynic acid (Edecrin).
Torsemide
Torsemide is sold as Demadex; furosemide is the loop diuretic sold as Lasix.
Ethacrynic acid
Ethacrynic acid is sold as Edecrin; furosemide is the loop diuretic sold as Lasix.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 12

loops1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: What happens to water in the descending limb of the loop of Henle?
opts: It stays in the lumen because the limb is impermeable
Impermeability to water describes the thick ascending limb. In the descending limb water leaves the lumen.
It enters the lumen from the interstitium
Water leaves the lumen in the descending limb rather than entering it, which concentrates the fluid left behind.
It leaves the lumen
Correct. Water leaves the lumen in the descending limb, which helps concentrate the urine; the ascending limb is the water-impermeable part.
It follows actively transported sodium out of the lumen
Active sodium reabsorption with an impermeable wall is the ascending limb; in the descending limb water simply leaves the lumen.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 9

loops1.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: A patient taking a loop diuretic is dizzy on standing and has dry mucous membranes. Which adverse effect is most likely?
opts: Hyperkalemia
Loop diuretics lower potassium, and hyperkalemia would not explain dry mucous membranes; this picture is volume depletion.
Hypermagnesemia
Loop diuretics increase magnesium loss, and hypermagnesemia does not explain dry membranes; this picture is volume depletion.
Volume depletion
Correct. Too much sodium and water loss leaves the patient volume depleted, with orthostatic dizziness and dry mucous membranes.
Fluid overload
Fluid overload gives edema and pulmonary congestion, the opposite of dry membranes and orthostasis; this picture is volume depletion.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 18

loops1.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which antibiotic class adds to the ototoxicity of loop diuretics?
opts: Penicillins
Penicillins are not described as potentiating ototoxicity; the antibiotic class that does so with loop diuretics is the aminoglycosides.
Cephalosporins
Cephalosporins are not described as potentiating ototoxicity; the antibiotic class that does so with loop diuretics is the aminoglycosides.
Monobactams
Monobactams are not described as potentiating ototoxicity; the antibiotic class that does so with loop diuretics is the aminoglycosides.
Aminoglycosides
Correct. Aminoglycosides potentiate the ototoxicity of loop diuretics, so the combination raises the risk of hearing damage.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 19

loops1.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which lipid change can loop diuretics cause through sympathetic activation?
opts: Higher triglycerides
Correct. Increased sympathetic activity raises triglycerides, a mild hyperlipidemia with loop diuretics.
Lower triglycerides
The effect is a rise in triglycerides; sympathetic activation does not lower them.
Lower low-density lipoprotein cholesterol
Loop diuretics do not lower low-density lipoprotein; the described effect is higher triglycerides.
Higher high-density lipoprotein cholesterol
Loop diuretics do not raise high-density lipoprotein; the described effect is higher triglycerides.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 16

loops1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which hormone rises as part of the compensation that blunts a diuretic and works to hold on to water?
opts: Atrial natriuretic peptide
Atrial natriuretic peptide falls, not rises, in diuretic braking; the water-retaining hormone that rises is antidiuretic hormone.
Parathyroid hormone
Parathyroid hormone regulates calcium and is not part of diuretic braking; antidiuretic hormone is the water-retaining hormone that rises.
Antidiuretic hormone
Correct. Antidiuretic hormone rises along with renin and aldosterone as part of diuretic braking, and it retains water.
Glucagon
Glucagon regulates blood glucose and is not part of diuretic braking; the water-retaining hormone that rises is antidiuretic hormone.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 5

loops1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which laboratory value is the diabetes-specific concern when a patient with diabetes starts a loop diuretic?
opts: Platelet count
Loop diuretics are not listed as affecting platelets; the diabetes-specific concern is a rise in blood glucose.
Serum bilirubin
Loop diuretics are not listed as affecting bilirubin; the diabetes-specific concern is a rise in blood glucose.
Serum amylase
Loop diuretics are not listed as affecting amylase; the diabetes-specific concern is a rise in blood glucose.
Blood glucose
Correct. Loop diuretics have diabetogenic effects, so blood glucose can rise and should be monitored.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 18

loops1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops1.q: Which transport protein do loop diuretics inhibit?
opts: Sodium-potassium-2-chloride carrier
Correct. Loop diuretics inhibit the sodium-potassium-2-chloride carrier on the luminal membrane of the thick ascending limb, trapping those ions in the urine.
The sodium-chloride transporter
The sodium-chloride transporter of the distal convoluted tubule is the thiazide target; loop diuretics block the sodium-potassium-2-chloride carrier.
The luminal sodium channel
Blocking the luminal sodium channel of the collecting duct is how amiloride and triamterene act; loop diuretics block the sodium-potassium-2-chloride carrier.
The sodium-hydrogen exchanger
The sodium-hydrogen exchange of the proximal tubule is reduced indirectly by carbonic anhydrase inhibitors; loop diuretics block the sodium-potassium-2-chloride carrier.
loops1.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 12

loops2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which adverse effect of loop diuretics can lead to cardiac arrhythmias?
opts: Hyponatremia
Hyponatremia from excess sodium loss is the effect that can lead to seizures, not arrhythmias.
Hyperuricemia
Hyperuricemia leads to gout, not arrhythmias; potassium loss is the cause of arrhythmias.
Azotemia
Azotemia is a rise in blood urea nitrogen; the effect that leads to arrhythmias is hypokalemia.
Hypokalemia
Correct. Loop diuretics increase potassium excretion, and the resulting hypokalemia can cause cardiac arrhythmias.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 18

loops2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which mediator is stimulated by loop diuretics and contributes to their vasodilator effect?
opts: Prostaglandin E2
Correct. Loop diuretics stimulate prostaglandin E2, which is why nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, which block prostaglandin synthesis, blunt the response.
Angiotensin II
Angiotensin II is a vasoconstrictor whose activity rises as a reflex; the vasodilator mediator stimulated by loop diuretics is prostaglandin E2.
Norepinephrine
Norepinephrine is released reflexly and constricts vessels; the vasodilator mediator stimulated by loop diuretics is prostaglandin E2.
Thromboxane A2
Thromboxane A2 is a vasoconstrictor and platelet activator; the vasodilator mediator stimulated by loop diuretics is prostaglandin E2.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 14

loops2.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Amiloride acts at which site?
opts: Distal convoluted tubule
The distal tubule is the thiazide site; potassium-sparing diuretics act in the collecting duct.
Proximal convoluted tubule
The proximal tubule is where carbonic anhydrase inhibitors act; potassium-sparing diuretics act in the collecting duct.
Collecting duct
Correct. Potassium-sparing diuretics act in the collecting duct, where about 2 to 3 percent of the sodium is reabsorbed under aldosterone control.
Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle
The thick ascending limb is the loop diuretic site; potassium-sparing diuretics act in the collecting duct.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 11

loops2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Where do loop diuretics interfere with the feedback signal that regulates glomerular filtration rate?
opts: The podocytes
Podocytes form the filtration barrier and do not generate the feedback signal; that signal arises at the macula densa.
The glomerular basement membrane
The basement membrane is part of the filtration barrier; loop diuretics alter the feedback signal at the macula densa.
The proximal tubule brush border
The brush border reabsorbs solutes; the transporter that loop diuretics block to alter the feedback signal is in the macula densa.
The macula densa
Correct. Loop diuretics block the transporter in the macula densa, altering the feedback signal that regulates filtration rate and angiotensin II.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 16

loops2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: A patient on furosemide has a high blood urea nitrogen with volume contraction. What is this adverse effect called?
opts: Hyperuricemia
Hyperuricemia is a high uric acid level that can cause gout; a high blood urea nitrogen is azotemia.
Contraction alkalosis
Contraction alkalosis is an acid-base change from volume loss; a high blood urea nitrogen is azotemia.
Hyperglycemia
Hyperglycemia is a raised blood glucose; a high blood urea nitrogen is azotemia.
Azotemia
Correct. Loop diuretics can cause azotemia, an increase in blood urea nitrogen, partly from the contraction of blood volume.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 18

loops2.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: How do loop diuretics interact with warfarin?
opts: They compete for plasma protein binding
Correct. Loop diuretics and warfarin compete for plasma protein binding, which can change the free warfarin level.
They induce warfarin metabolism in the liver
Loop diuretics are not listed as enzyme inducers; the described interaction is competition for plasma protein binding.
They block vitamin K recycling
Blocking vitamin K recycling is the warfarin mechanism itself; the loop diuretic interaction is competition for plasma protein binding.
They increase warfarin excretion in urine
The described interaction is competition for plasma protein binding, not faster renal excretion of warfarin.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 19

loops2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: A patient on a loop diuretic develops hearing loss. Which structure is damaged?
opts: The tympanic membrane
The tympanic membrane is not the target of loop diuretic ototoxicity; the damage is to hair cells in the cochlea.
The ossicles of the middle ear
The ossicles transmit sound and are not injured by loop diuretics; the damage is to hair cells in the cochlea.
Hair cells in the cochlea
Correct. Loop diuretic ototoxicity comes from damage to the hair cells of the cochlea.
The eustachian tube
The eustachian tube equalizes pressure and is not injured; loop diuretics damage hair cells in the cochlea.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 18

loops2.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which condition is treated with a loop diuretic given together with saline?
opts: Hypercalcemia
Correct. Loop diuretics increase calcium excretion, so with saline they are used to treat hypercalcemia.
Hypocalcemia
Loop diuretics increase calcium loss and would worsen low calcium; with saline they treat hypercalcemia.
Hypokalemia
Loop diuretics cause potassium loss and would worsen hypokalemia; with saline they treat hypercalcemia.
Hyponatremia
Loop diuretics can themselves cause hyponatremia; the condition they treat with saline is hypercalcemia.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 17

loops2.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which electrolyte excretion do loop diuretics increase but thiazide diuretics decrease?
opts: Potassium
Both loop diuretics and thiazides increase potassium excretion, so it does not separate them; calcium does.
Magnesium
Both classes increase magnesium excretion; the electrolyte that is increased by loops and decreased by thiazides is calcium.
Calcium
Correct. Loop diuretics increase calcium (and magnesium) excretion, whereas thiazides decrease renal calcium excretion.
Sodium
Both classes increase sodium excretion, which is what makes them diuretics; calcium is the one they handle oppositely.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 13

loops2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: What is the danger of a sustained excess loss of sodium and chloride?
opts: Volume overload and pulmonary edema
Volume overload with pulmonary edema comes from too much sodium and fluid on board, the opposite of an excess loss.
Hypertensive crisis from fluid retention
Fluid retention comes from sodium excess, not loss; a sustained excess loss lowers volume and risks cardiovascular collapse.
Hypernatremia with confusion
Diuretic sodium loss tends to lower sodium; the sustained danger of losing too much sodium and chloride is volume depletion and cardiovascular collapse.
Volume depletion and cardiovascular collapse
Correct. Too little sodium and chloride in the body means too little volume, so volume depletion and cardiovascular collapse can follow.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 4

loops2.io: Identify indications for commonly used diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which acute condition is relieved because a loop diuretic lowers pulmonary pressure?
opts: Pulmonary edema
Correct. Loop diuretics reduce pulmonary pressure and are used for pulmonary edema.
Pulmonary embolism
A pulmonary embolism is a clot in the pulmonary vessels; the condition relieved by lowering pulmonary pressure with a loop diuretic is pulmonary edema.
Asthma exacerbation
An asthma exacerbation is airway narrowing; the condition relieved by lowering pulmonary pressure with a loop diuretic is pulmonary edema.
Pneumothorax
A pneumothorax is air in the pleural space; the condition relieved by lowering pulmonary pressure with a loop diuretic is pulmonary edema.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 17

loops2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which mechanism contributes to hyperglycemia with loop diuretics?
opts: Increased renal glucose reabsorption
Loop diuretics do not alter renal glucose handling; hyperglycemia comes from impaired insulin release and insulin resistance.
Increased insulin secretion
Insulin release falls, not rises, in this setting; hypokalemia impairs insulin release and drives hyperglycemia.
Hypokalemia impairs insulin release
Correct. Potassium loss impairs insulin release, and reflex catecholamines and impaired peripheral glucose uptake add to the rise in blood glucose.
Reduced glucose filtration at the glomerulus
Glucose handling at the glomerulus is not the mechanism; hypokalemia impairing insulin release is.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 14

loops2.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which diuretic class produces the largest urine output?
opts: Thiazide diuretics
Thiazides raise urine output only modestly, about 1 to 2 liters per day, because they act where far less sodium is reabsorbed.
Loop diuretics
Correct. Loop diuretics are the most potent class, with urine output up to about 4 liters per day because they block the segment that reabsorbs the most sodium beyond the proximal tubule.
Potassium-sparing diuretics
Potassium-sparing diuretics have only a modest effect on urine flow; their main value is holding on to potassium.
Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors
Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors are weak diuretics whose sodium loss wanes within days; loop diuretics give the largest output.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 13

loops2.io: Describe adverse effects of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which skin-related adverse effects can occur with loop diuretics?
opts: Alopecia and nail ridging
These are not listed adverse effects of loop diuretics; the skin effects are rash and photosensitivity.
Rash and photosensitivity
Correct. Allergic reactions with a rash and photosensitivity are listed adverse effects of loop diuretics.
Vitiligo and hyperhidrosis
These are not adverse effects of loop diuretics; the skin effects are an allergic rash and photosensitivity.
Gingival overgrowth and hirsutism
These belong to other drugs; the skin effects of loop diuretics are rash and photosensitivity.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 18

loops2.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Furosemide acts at which site?
opts: Proximal convoluted tubule
The proximal tubule is the site of carbonic anhydrase inhibitors; loop diuretics act on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.
Distal convoluted tubule
The distal tubule is the site of thiazide diuretics; loop diuretics act on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.
Collecting duct
The collecting duct is the site of potassium-sparing diuretics; loop diuretics act on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.
Thick ascending limb
Correct. Loop diuretics work in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, where about 25 percent of the sodium is reabsorbed.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 12

loops2.io: Outline appropriate patient education for diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which new symptom should a patient on a loop diuretic report promptly?
opts: Increased urine volume
Increased urine output is the expected action of the drug and is not a warning sign.
New hearing loss
Correct. Ototoxicity from hair cell damage in the cochlea is a loop diuretic adverse effect, so hearing changes should be reported.
Loss of excess fluid weight
Weight loss from fluid removal is the intended effect and is not a warning sign.
Less ankle swelling
Reduced swelling is the intended benefit and is not a warning sign.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 18

loops2.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which drug is NOT a loop diuretic?
opts: Ethacrynic acid
Ethacrynic acid (Edecrin) is a loop diuretic even though its name does not follow the usual naming pattern.
Chlorthalidone
Correct. Chlorthalidone (Hygroton) is a thiazide-type diuretic; the loop diuretics are furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide and ethacrynic acid.
Torsemide
Torsemide (Demadex) is a loop diuretic that acts on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.
Furosemide
Furosemide (Lasix) is the prototype loop diuretic that inhibits the sodium-potassium-2-chloride carrier.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 12

loops2.io: Identify diuretics and heart failure drug classes and commonly prescribed diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which diuretic continues to work when creatinine clearance falls below 30 milliliters per minute?
opts: Acetazolamide
Acetazolamide is a weak diuretic whose sodium loss fades within days; the drug that remains effective at low clearance is a loop diuretic.
Furosemide
Correct. Furosemide, like the other loop diuretics, remains effective in patients whose creatinine clearance is below 30 milliliters per minute.
Amiloride
Amiloride is only a modest diuretic whose main concern is hyperkalemia; the drug that remains effective at low clearance is a loop diuretic.
Spironolactone
Spironolactone blocks only 2 to 3 percent of sodium reabsorption and raises potassium; the drug that remains effective at low clearance is a loop diuretic.
loops2.cite: Diuretics and Heart Failure Drugs.pptx, Slide 16

loops2.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which drug class blunts the natriuretic and blood pressure response to loop diuretics?
opts: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
Correct. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs block the prostaglandins that contribute to the natriuretic and blood pressure response of loop diuretics.
Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors
These inhibitors add to the blood pressure effect rather than blunting it; the drugs that blunt the natriuretic response are the nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.
Calcium channel blockers
Calcium channel blockers do not blunt loop diuretic natriuresis; nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs do by blocking prostaglandins.
Proton pump inhibitors
Proton pump inhibitors do not blunt loop diuretic natriuresis; nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs do by blocking prostaglandins.

loops2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which hormone controls the water channels of the collecting duct?
opts: Aldosterone
Aldosterone acts on an intracellular receptor to increase sodium channels and the sodium-potassium pump; antidiuretic hormone controls the water channels.
Angiotensin II
Angiotensin II stimulates aldosterone release and vasoconstriction; the collecting duct water channels are controlled by antidiuretic hormone.
Antidiuretic hormone
Correct. Antidiuretic hormone acts on its receptor to insert water channel molecules into the luminal membrane of the collecting duct.
Atrial natriuretic peptide
Atrial natriuretic peptide promotes sodium excretion and is not what inserts water channels; antidiuretic hormone does.

loops2.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Why does a loop diuretic raise the arrhythmia risk of digoxin?
opts: It raises potassium and calcium
Loop diuretics lower potassium and increase calcium loss; the problem is low potassium and magnesium.
It lowers potassium and magnesium
Correct. Loop diuretics cause hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia, and low potassium and magnesium make digoxin arrhythmias more likely.
It slows digoxin absorption from the gut
That would lower digoxin effect rather than raise arrhythmia risk; the interaction is electrolyte loss.
It blocks digoxin binding to its pump
That would reduce digoxin action; the interaction is arrhythmia risk from low potassium and magnesium.

loops2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of diuretics and heart failure drugs
loops2.q: Which solutes are normally reabsorbed in the proximal tubule so that they do not appear in urine?
opts: Glucose and amino acids
Correct. The proximal tubule reabsorbs glucose, amino acids and organic solutes, which is why they are normally absent from urine.
Antidiuretic hormone and aldosterone
These are hormones that act on the collecting duct; the proximal tubule reabsorbs glucose, amino acids and organic solutes.
Sodium only, with no organic solutes
The proximal tubule also reclaims organic solutes: glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed there so they do not appear in urine.
Weak acids and weak bases
Weak acids and bases are excreted into the lumen at the proximal tubule, not reabsorbed; glucose and amino acids are the solutes reabsorbed.
